title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Wang Chung Village was such a famous village. I have also heard many things about its pearl rice. Can you tell me any more about this?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Wang Chung Village很有名，我亦聽過不少珍珠米的事，可多說一點嗎？

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Well, I remember my father would have buyers for this rice from all over China. But it wasn’t just him. All the farmers in our village did this. Our rice was in huge demand then, you know. Pearl rice was not cheap. It was a luxury even for rich families.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 記得父親的米有中國各地買家，不只他，全村農民都是。當年需求很大，珍珠米不便宜，連富裕家庭也視為奢侈品。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Sadly, of course, we can’t see the village anymore, but can you describe what it was like?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Ah well, our village was so beautiful. Tourists from the city would come at the weekend to see the rice fields.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Yes, the “S”-shaped fields. I’ve some photos of them. Truly beautiful.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I remember the great flood of Wang Chung Village, you know.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Really? Typhoon Ellen in 1983?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I think so. The two girls who survived on the kitchen cupboard? I knew them. Good little girls. Very pious. Their mother told me about what happened.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 應該是。靠廚櫃生還的兩個女孩？我認識她們，是虔誠的好孩子。母親告訴我經過。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Did she tell you about the markings on the cupboard door?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Yes. A prayer, a prayer to Guanyin.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Well, I’ll be. The Goddess of Mercy. They carved it on the right door of the cupboard?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: No, she told me it was the left. They carved it when they were waiting to be rescued.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Oh really? My mistake then. Now, after 1990 you moved to your present home in Fanling. Was that a big change?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 真的？我記錯了。1990年後搬到粉嶺現在的家，改變大嗎？

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Well, of course there were some things from before that I missed a lot. Especially to begin with. The first few years I found it quite difficult to adapt to city life. But Fanling is a lovely place. There’s so much I can do here. I’m a member of the residents’ association on the estate. I am really involved in that and I like helping others on the estate. You might not believe it but I’m 79 this year. But there are others younger than me that need help so I do all I can. And in the end it’s family and friends that are important and I’m lucky. I have 14 grandchildren and one great granddaughter. I had family and friends in Wang Chung and still have them now I’m in Fanling.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 當然很想念昔日一些事，尤其最初幾年，很難適應城市生活。但粉嶺很好，有很多事可做。我是屋苑居民協會成員，積極參與，喜歡助人。你可能不信，我今年79歲，但還有比我年輕的人需要幫助，我便盡力。最重要是親友，我很幸運，有14名孫兒女及一名曾孫女。以前村裏有親友，現在粉嶺亦有。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: The death and destruction brought by Typhoon Ellen had a happy twist in its tornado’s tale yesterday when two young sisters were miraculously found alive after fears the pair had drowned. Man Yee (7) and Man Ching (9) Lee were found clinging to the family’s kitchen cupboard as it floated in flood waters. They had survived for two days on the wooden cupboard while waiting for help after their home had been struck by a flash flood.

text: I am writing on behalf of The Committee for Hong Kong International Primary Schools to make known to you the concerns we have about school visits to the Social History Museum.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: First, I would like to draw your attention to concerns I have about how safe your museum is for children. But first, I’ll be interviewing a very different doctor. I have with me today Dr. Jack Jones from the Hong Kong Social History Museum. Dr. Jones, welcome back to Nosing Around. Patty Leung: So, maybe we can start with the Social History Museum. I’m sure our listeners know what a museum is traditionally, but can you explain what a social history museum is? Dr. Jones: Well, Patty, that’s a good question. A social history museum is a place where visitors can experience what daily life was like for ordinary people in the past. Patty Leung: OK. Dr. Jones: Yes, ordinary people like you and me, not kings and queens. You’re not a queen, I’m guessing. Patty Leung: (laughs) Well, maybe in a past life. Now, we are here to discuss Bubblegum’s visit to Hong Kong. Let’s start with the first two things then. Okay, so on the first day Bubblegum have their performance at Atlantic Plaza, and then on the 19th they are making a music video for the song “Around the World with You.” Let’s start by talking about the performance at Atlantic Plaza. Now Starsky, I’ve put this down in my calendar for the 18th of May—on the Monday. Starsky: Okay, Atlantic Plaza, Monday, May… Did you say the 18th? Malcolm: Yes, that’s right—the 18th of May. Make sure you put that in the schedule. Starsky: Yes, I will. Malcolm: Good. Now Starsky, it’s really important for the band to practise before the actual performance at Atlantic Plaza. So make sure you tell them in the schedule to practise their songs. Let’s see now—the performance is at 2:30 pm, so I want them to practise from 10 am until lunch time. Starsky: Okay. I will tell them to practise their songs at 10 am at Atlantic Plaza and practise until it’s time for lunch.

text: Malcolm: And one more thing. I’ve changed my mind about the song list for Atlantic Plaza. Make sure the band sing their song “Look at Me” as the sixth and final song. text: Malcolm：還有，我改了Atlantic Plaza歌單，要把《Look at Me》放在第六首、即最後一首。這是好歌，「看着我，看着我，耶耶……」 Starsky：好的，放在歌單最後。 音樂影片討論 Malcolm：Eduardo，談談《Around the World with You》的影片，你有甚麼想法？ Eduardo：計劃在世界著名地標拍Bubblegum。 Malcolm：明白，歌名是「和你環遊世界」，所以在各地地標拍攝。 Eduardo：對，紐約已安排好。 Malcolm：香港呢？想好地點嗎？ Eduardo：The Peak Sky Deck，很完美。 Malcolm：甚麼？ Eduardo：The Peak Sky Deck，就是香港山頂那幢建築。 Malcolm：我知道，算是著名旅遊點，至少在香港。順帶問噪音水平呢？最好安靜些。 Eduardo：不會嘈吵，只用小型CD機，樂隊對着CD對嘴演出。

text: Malcolm: Good. We don’t want to have all the millionaires on the Peak getting mad at us! Ha ha. Interview Rules Malcolm: Now, Starsky, before I forget. Did I mention that a local Hong Kong school asked me if they could interview the band? Starsky: Yes. I remember you mentioning it. Malcolm: Well, I’ve agreed to it. But we need to be careful that the publicity is good for us, so you need to tell this school—or anyone else who wants an interview—that we have certain rules. Starsky: You mean no questions about boyfriends or girlfriends? Malcolm: Exactly—strictly no questions about the love lives of the band: boyfriends, girlfriends, whatever. And all interviews must take place in the hotel. We want to control the situation as much as possible. Hotel or nothing. I’ll send you the emails and other details to help you write the reply. Merchandise Discussion Starsky: Oh, I wanted to ask—will we need to order up any merchandise and souvenirs for Bubblegum’s Asian tour? Malcolm: That’s a good point, Starsky. I’ll email you about that later too. But it’s important to note that whatever souvenirs we do order, we will need at least 20,000 of each item, and they will need to be ready by the beginning of May. Starsky: 20,000. Wow. First week of May. That’s quite soon then. Malcolm: Yeah. We’ve been looking at the Bubblegum MyFace page and the fans say they want clothes. Starsky: Mm. Well, we can do a whole range of stuff like baseball caps, T-shirts, hoodies. Malcolm: No, no. Let’s keep it simple and just go for T-shirts. They’re always the best sellers.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Good morning everyone, thanks to everyone for coming this morning. The International Airport Committee is pleased to announce the winners of the Best International Airport Award for 2012. The competition was close this year, with some airports showing a big improvement on the figures from 2011. Congratulations go to Hong Kong for winning first prize. We all know the airport at Chek Lap Kok is always a popular choice with world travellers. Moving up from third place last year to second place this year is Singapore, very well done to them. Finally, we award Seoul’s Incheon airport in South Korea, which claims third place. A special thank you must go to all the world travellers who voted in this year’s competition and our hearty congratulations to the winners. Now, are there any questions?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: We’ve all heard of student gap years, you know, where students take a year off and travel and that. Some go to places like South America and live with the natives – even for like up to a year. But did you know that there are more people going to live with native tribes in countries in Africa – but only for a few weeks? Welcome to a really new kind of culture tourism. I’m in Kenya and I’m going to a small village called Sauri, to find out what the impact might be on local people…

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 大家都聽過學生間隔年，就是休學一年去旅行之類。有些人到南美洲等地與原住民同住，甚至長達一年。但你知道愈來愈多人到非洲國家與原住部族一起住，只住幾星期嗎？歡迎認識這種很新的文化旅遊。我在肯尼亞，正前往 Sauri 小村，了解這對當地居民可能有何影響……

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: [Ceci Yip video clip – extract 2]

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I’ve got with me now Kemi – Kemi, you’re a teacher here in Sauri, what do you think about the effect of tourism on local people?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 現在 Kemi 在我身旁。Kemi，你是 Sauri 的老師，你認為旅遊對居民有何影響？

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I think generally Ceci that it’s a good thing. I’d say positive for Sauri on the whole.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Ceci，我認為整體是好事，對 Sauri 大致有正面影響。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Really? Well, that’s encouraging. How do you mean positive?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Well, for example, in Sauri people are starting to share ideas with tourists.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Oh really? You mean sharing practical ideas?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Yes, last year a young man from Turkey – Yusuf – came to the village. And helped us create a village webpage. So we have the Sauri village homepage on the Internet. It’s got a lot of information about the village that visitors can read.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 對，去年一位土耳其青年 Yusuf 來到村裏，幫我們建立村落網頁。因此網上有 Sauri 村首頁，提供很多村落資料供遊客閱讀。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I heard that there was a writer who came to the village…

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Yes, yes, a very nice lady called Mrs. Jessica Glasser. We have a great tradition of story-telling and together with the local people Mrs. Glasser wrote down some of the stories and helped us to get those published. So that anybody who reads the book learns about our traditions.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 是的，一位很親切的女士 Jessica Glasser。我們有豐富的講故事傳統，她與居民一起把一些故事記下並協助出版，讓讀者了解我們的傳統。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: So it really does sound like tourism is helping you keep your culture alive. In a real way.

text: Asia Life 三月號刊登的 Kevin Hui 來信

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I’m writing about the effects of tourism. I used to be a travel agent and I’ve travelled to many different places in the world because of my job and I have observed that the effects of tourism are increasingly negative.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 我寫信談旅遊的影響。我曾是旅行社職員，因工作到過世界很多地方，觀察到旅遊的負面影響日益增加。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Recently, the Brazilian government discovered a ‘lost tribe’ of people living deep inside the rainforest. Instead of using the tribe to generate more tourism as we have seen in so many other countries, they have decided to leave the tribes of people uncontacted. The government even has guards to stop everyone, especially tourists, going into those areas to contact the tribes.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 最近巴西政府發現雨林深處一個「失落部族」。他們沒有像許多國家般利用部族吸引遊客，而是決定不與這些部族接觸，甚至安排守衛阻止任何人，尤其遊客，進入那些地區接觸部族。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I couldn’t agree more with this decision. Now, these tribal groups can live immersed in their own traditions and without being negatively influenced by anyone from outside their own community or country.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 我完全贊同。這些部族現在可以沉浸於自身傳統生活，不受社區或國家以外的人負面影響。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: There’s some good news this week!! I sat next to a girl called Ka Man in class, but she told me to call her Carmen. She seemed a bit shy but she asked me about Nepal and how it is different from Hong Kong. Then, my teacher asked me to do a presentation about Nepal to my class next week. I’m going to show some photos and play some music too! I did a practice run and she gave me some tips about body language like paying attention to how I stand. She said that if I put my hands on my hips when I present I look over-confident – a bit arrogant. She told me to relax my arms and let them hang by my side…I think I need to practise ;-).

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 今個星期有好消息！！我上課坐在一位叫 Ka Man 的女生旁邊，但她叫我稱呼她 Carmen。她似乎有點害羞，卻問我尼泊爾的情況，以及它跟香港的分別。然後老師請我下星期向全班介紹尼泊爾。我會展示照片，也會播放音樂！我試講了一次，她給我一些身體語言的建議，例如留意站姿。她說演講時雙手叉腰會顯得過分自信，有點傲慢。她叫我放鬆雙臂，讓它們自然垂在身旁……我想我需要練習 ;-).

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Extract from Isobel Tait’s article ‘A Review of Research into Body Language’

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Isobel Tait 的文章《身體語言研究回顧》節錄

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: There is sufficient evidence at this stage to safely conclude that certain aspects of body language can have both positive and negative effects on the perceptions of others in a variety of contexts and cultures (Lo, 1999; Lo and Francis, 2001). It has even been argued that body language is the most important aspect of human communication (Duncan, 2004).

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 現階段已有足夠證據，可以穩妥地斷定：在不同情境及文化中，某些身體語言會對他人的觀感產生正面或負面影響（Lo，1999；Lo 及 Francis，2001）。甚至有人主張，身體語言是人類溝通最重要的部分（Duncan，2004）。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: De Frietas (2006), for example, found that how people stand has a significant effect on listeners’ perceptions of the speaker when giving presentations. She found that in a job interview situation, candidates actually failed the interview based on the way that they stood when asked to give a presentation.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 例如，De Frietas（2006）發現，演講者的站姿會顯著影響聽眾對他的觀感。她發現，在求職面試中，有應徵者被要求作匯報時，竟因站姿而未能通過面試。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Amocatchi (2008) conducted a survey, in which she showed over 1,000 different people a drawing of someone folding their arms. She asked them what kind of message they thought was being transmitted. The results can be seen in Figure 2 below. Amocatchi concludes that the best advice for listeners is to avoid confusion by reverting to a neutral position, i.e. with their hands loosely clasped in front of them.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Amocatchi（2008）進行調查，向超過 1,000 人展示一幅有人雙臂交叉的圖畫，詢問他們認為這個姿勢傳達甚麼訊息。結果見下方圖 2。Amocatchi 的結論是：聽眾最好回復中立姿勢，即雙手在身前輕輕交握，以免造成誤會。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Figure 1: Folded arms (Amocatchi, 2008)

title: Data File / 原題目及練習

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 43% is not a majority. Use “some people” and “can mean”, not “most people” or a claim that crossed arms always mean agreement.

text: Article from Living in Hong Kong newsletter

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Imagine waking up in a brand new country. Have you ever wondered what that might feel like? This month, three recent arrivals in Hong Kong – Mina, Georg and Tariq – talked about their new lives in Hong Kong.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 想像在全新的國家醒來，你有沒有想過是甚麼感受？本月三位新來港人士 Mina、Georg 及 Tariq，分享他們在香港的新生活。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: First of all, welcome to Hong Kong. How long have you been here and what are you doing here?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Well, Georg and I are students at Kowloon University and we’ve been here for three months.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Georg 和我是 Kowloon University 的學生，來了三個月。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I’m originally from Oman and I’ve come to live with my grandparents and help in the family business. I’ve been here for two months.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 我本來住在阿曼，來這裏與祖父母同住，幫忙打理家族生意。我來了兩個月。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Are you enjoying life in Hong Kong?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Yes, we all think it’s a great place – for me, it’s very different from Sweden which is where I come from.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 喜歡，我們都覺得這裏很好。對我來說，香港跟我的家鄉瑞典很不同。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: We wanted to ask you today about communication in Hong Kong. Have you come across any barriers?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: The pace of life here is so fast, everyone seems to be in a hurry and they don’t seem to have the time to talk to you. So I guess time is a barrier.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 這裏生活節奏太快，人人似乎都很匆忙，好像沒有時間跟你交談。所以我想時間是一個障礙。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: I know just what you mean, like when I was in a shop last week, I was trying to ask about the price of something and the shop assistant wouldn’t take the time to answer my questions. It was really frustrating.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 我完全明白。上星期我在商店想問一件貨品的價錢，店員卻不肯花時間回答，真的令人沮喪。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Frustrating for you, but ultimately businesses suffer because you end up going to another shop and the first shop loses custom.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Noise as well can be a real barrier. I have had several instances when I’ve received a phone call when I was on a big busy road, like Nathan Road or somewhere, and I simply couldn’t understand what was being said. On one occasion it was an important phone call about a job interview I’d attended and I just couldn’t catch what was being said.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 噪音也是實在的障礙。我曾多次在彌敦道之類繁忙大馬路上接到電話，卻完全聽不清楚。有一次是關於我參加過的求職面試的重要來電，我就是聽不到對方說甚麼。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Is there anything that you’ve found difficult about living in Hong Kong?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: At first I couldn’t find a doctor but then someone told me about some free clinics near where I live in Mongkok. There are four of them offering free clinics once a week.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Not really – sometimes I miss the food from home, but then I found a website which gave me information about shops which sell food from Sweden and a list of restaurants I can go to. It’s great.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Kowloon Herald 2012 年 2 月 15 日文章

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Local lawyers, Venny Wong and Theresa Lam, who both work at law firm Chan and Wang Legal Company, have taken the decision to provide pro bono services to newcomers coming to live in Hong Kong through a community-based legal advice scheme.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 任職 Chan and Wang Legal Company 的本地律師 Venny Wong 和 Theresa Lam，決定透過社區法律諮詢計劃，為新來港定居人士提供免費法律服務。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: “We realised that there are some people who come to live in Hong Kong who need a bit of extra help,” explained Venny Wong. “They arrive in a new country and face practical difficulties like dealing with immigration or finding legal advice for other matters. Often they can’t afford that advice.”

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Venny Wong 解釋：「我們發現，有些來港定居的人需要多一點幫助。他們到了新地方，面對處理入境事宜或尋求其他法律意見等實際困難，而且往往無力支付費用。」

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Both Venny and Theresa have decided to try to build up a network to encourage others to do more.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Venny 和 Theresa 決定嘗試建立支援網絡，鼓勵更多人出力。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Theresa explains, “We’re already talking to friends from other businesses to see if they want to help.”

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Theresa 解釋：「我們已聯絡其他行業的朋友，看看他們是否願意幫忙。」

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: In fact, they’ve already had some success. Enrique Ramirez, an estate agent in Kwun Tong, is offering a helping hand. “We provide a commission-free service to help newcomers to find somewhere to live in Hong Kong. So far we’ve helped about 20 families,” he explained.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 事實上，已有一些成果。觀塘地產代理 Enrique Ramirez 正提供協助。他說：「我們提供免佣服務，幫助新來港人士在香港找到住所。至今已協助約 20 個家庭。」

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Government organizations are also doing their bit to help. The Hong Kong Tourism Board has recently produced a new MTR map for tourists and newcomers. “It will help people new to Hong Kong find their way round so they can shop till they drop,” a spokeswoman announced.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 政府機構也出一分力。香港旅遊發展局最近為遊客和新來港人士製作新版港鐵路線圖。女發言人表示：「這有助初到香港的人認路，讓他們盡情購物。」

text: 2012 Podcast Transcript – Bookmark with Arlene Lee and Lionel Chan Part B Arlene Lee: I’m Arlene Lee. Welcome to this week’s Bookmark, and we’re delighted to have Lionel Chan as our special guest today. Welcome, Lionel. Lionel Chan: Thank you, it’s great to be here. Arlene Lee: We’re going to talk about your new book today, but before we do that, I know you’d like to mention an important community event that’s happening soon. Lionel Chan: OK, yeah, it’s a Fun Day. And it’s taking place in Kowloon Park on the 15th of April. There’ll be lots of people from different countries there. Arlene Lee: OK, so if we want to come along, we need to get down to Kowloon Park on the 15th of April. Is that a Saturday or a Sunday? Lionel Chan: The 15th’s a Sunday, Arlene. Arlene Lee: Right. So what will be happening at the Fun Day? Lionel Chan: There’ll be lots of activities—like a lucky draw. Arlene Lee: Great. I love lucky draws. Lionel Chan: Yeah, but don’t just come for the lucky draw. I think the Fun Day’s actually very important. It’s a great chance for people from different cultures to meet each other.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 2012 播客逐字稿：Bookmark，主持 Arlene Lee，嘉賓 Lionel Chan。乙部。 Arlene：我是 Arlene Lee。歡迎收聽本週 Bookmark。今天很高興請來特別嘉賓 Lionel Chan，歡迎你。 Lionel：謝謝，很高興來到這裏。 Arlene：我們今天會談談你的新書。不過首先，你想說說即將舉行的重要社區活動。 Lionel：是的，4 月 15 日九龍公園有同樂日，來自很多不同國家的人都會參加。 Arlene：所以 4 月 15 日要到九龍公園。那天是星期六還是星期日？ Lionel：15 日是星期日，Arlene。 Arlene：當天會有甚麼活動？ Lionel：很多，例如幸運抽獎。 Arlene：太好了，我很喜歡抽獎。 Lionel：不要只為抽獎而來。同樂日很重要，讓不同文化背景的人有機會見面。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 2012 播客逐字稿：Arlene Lee 與 Lionel Chan

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Arlene Lee: So a lucky draw and a chance to meet people from different cultures. Sounds good. And will you be there? Lionel Chan: Yeah, I’ll be there. Another one of the activities at the Fun Day is I’m giving a talk about body language. Arlene Lee: A talk about body language? Is there much to say about body language then? Lionel Chan: Well, yeah. Yes, there is. We communicate using our bodies and it’s something we really should be more aware of. Arlene Lee: OK, like what for example? Lionel Chan: Well, the classic example is eye contact. Eye contact is the aspect of nonverbal communication that varies most from country to country. Arlene Lee: Really? Lionel Chan: Yes, for example the length of time that people’s eyes meet. If your eyes meet with someone for a long time, it can mean at least three different things depending on the country. Arlene Lee: Three different things? Lionel Chan: Yeah. For example, in some countries it means you want a fight. Arlene Lee: So too much eye contact can mean a sort of challenge, is that it? Lionel Chan: Well, yeah. But in other countries it can mean something totally different. It can also mean that you are showing that you are really interested in what the person is saying. Arlene Lee: Right. And the third?

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Arlene：有抽獎，又可以認識其他文化的人，聽起來很好。你會到場嗎？ Lionel：會，我會作一個身體語言講座。 Arlene：身體語言有那麼多值得說的嗎？ Lionel：我們會用身體溝通，應該更留意這一點。 Arlene：可以舉個例子吗？ Lionel：一個典型例子是眼神接觸，這是各國差異最大的非語言溝通方式之一。 Arlene：真的嗎？ Lionel：就是雙方目光接觸多久。長時間注視，視乎國家，可有至少三種意思。 Arlene：三種？ Lionel：在某些國家，表示你想打架。 Arlene：所以過多眼神接觸是一種挑釁？ Lionel：對。但在其他地方，意思完全不同，代表你對對方所說的話很感興趣。 Arlene：第三種呢？

text: Lionel Chan: Yes, right, well, the third possible meaning of a long meeting of the eyes is, of course, romantic—that you’re interested in that person romantically. Arlene Lee: Well, there’s a bit of a difference there then! You want a fight, you’re interested, or you want to be his girlfriend! Lionel Chan: Exactly. Arlene Lee: And can you give some advice to people about eye contact then? Lionel Chan: Well, I think the best advice is to try to become aware of what you do yourself and adapt to the situation. Arlene Lee: Sounds like good advice: become aware of what I do with my eyes and adapt to the situation I’m in! Lionel Chan: (laughs) Yes, that’s it! Arlene Lee: Now, Lionel, we know that you’ll be giving a talk at the Fun Day, but some of our listeners might not know that much about you. Could you tell us something about yourself? Lionel Chan: Well, I was actually born in Singapore but came here as a young man. And when I first arrived in Hong Kong I got a job as a social worker— Arlene Lee: Oh really? I always thought you were from Hong Kong. Lionel Chan: No. No. Singapore. Arlene Lee: OK, my mistake. And how long were you a social worker? Lionel Chan: Oh, for about 10 years, I suppose.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Lionel：第三種是你對對方有愛慕之意。 Arlene：分別很大：想打架、感兴趣，還是想當對方女朋友！ Lionel：正是如此。 Arlene：那有甚麼建議？ Lionel：留意自己的行為，按情境作調整。 Arlene：好建議，要留意自己的眼睛，然後調整。 Lionel：（笑）沒錯！ Arlene：有些聽眾可能不認識你，可以介紹一下自己嗎？ Lionel：我在新加坡出生，年輕時來香港。第一份工作是社工。 Arlene：我以為你在香港出生。 Lionel：不是，是新加坡。 Arlene：是我弄錯了。你做了多久社工？ Lionel：大約十年。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 2012 播客逐字稿：Arlene Lee 與 Lionel Chan

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Arlene Lee: Well, 10 years is quite a long time in a job like that. Lionel Chan: Mm. Arlene Lee: I’m always interested to read what you have to say about communication barriers and how they affect us. I’m interested to know, what about those barriers that are particular to Hong Kong or barriers that are a real problem in Hong Kong compared to other places? Lionel Chan: I’m not sure if these are unique to Hong Kong, but the barriers to communication that people mention when they’ve just arrived in Hong Kong are: noise, time and people not listening. Arlene Lee: Yeah, I can imagine that. Noise, time and people not listening sounds like Hong Kong on a bad day! Lionel Chan: Well, yes. It might be quite amusing but these are all genuine barriers to communication in Hong Kong. They all prevent communication—and that’s what a barrier is. A barrier stops something from happening. Arlene Lee: Mm. OK, so a barrier stops something from happening. Right. Lionel Chan: And the important thing is what happens next. As I say, a barrier like noise stops communication happening, but it’s how that affects people—that’s the point. Take noise as an example. We all know Hong Kong can be very noisy. But what happens when it’s so noisy that we just can’t communicate? Arlene Lee: I know I just get angry. Lionel Chan: Well, you’re not alone, Arlene. There’s been quite a lot of research into this area, you know, monitoring people’s blood pressure and so on, and all the research points towards noise as a communication barrier adding significantly to people’s stress levels. Arlene Lee: OK, I’ll have to look for a quiet space to talk then! Lionel Chan: Mm.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Arlene：十年，同一份工作做了很久。 Lionel：嗯。 Arlene：我很感興趣，讀到關於溝通障礙及其影響的內容。有沒有哪種障礙是香港特有，或比其他地方更嚴重的？ Lionel：我不確定是否香港獨有，但新來港人士會提到噪音、時間和人們不聆聽。 Arlene：聽起來像香港糟糕的一天！ Lionel：聽來有趣，但的確是問題，會妨礙溝通。障礙就是阻止事情發生的事物。 Arlene：對，障礙會阻止事情。 Lionel：重要的是接下來的影響。噪音會阻礙溝通，但重點是它對人的影響。香港很嘈吵，無法溝通時會怎樣？ Arlene：我會生氣。 Lionel：不只你一個。許多血壓等研究顯示，壓力會顯著增加。 Arlene：那就一定要找個安靜地方談話。 Lionel：嗯。

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: Arlene Lee: You mentioned newcomers arriving in Hong Kong. You mean people from outside China. Lionel Chan: Yes, well, the people I meet in Hong Kong are from everywhere—from Africa, from South America, from the Middle East… These people come to Hong Kong to start new lives. Just like I did. Some people need help to deal with the practical difficulties. Arlene Lee: What kinds of difficulties do they need help with? Lionel Chan: Well, things like finding schools for their children. There are two difficulties here: firstly to find a school, and secondly to fill in the school application form. Some newcomers don’t really have the written skills in English or Chinese to fill in those long government forms. Arlene Lee: Yeah, well, I find filling in those forms bad enough. But if it’s something as important as finding a school for their children, then that sounds like something really worthwhile to do. Lionel Chan: Mm. Arlene Lee: OK. text: The chart really speaks for itself in terms of the profound impact of parents being involved in their child’s school life. title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: The study states that a big benefit is the atmosphere it creates for students. At school, students only get one type of adult interaction: with their teachers. When you get parents in the mix at school, students then get to interact with other adults. The atmosphere created makes students feel more relaxed during school events. We know what that means for students: less depression and, naturally, less anxiety.

title: Data File / 原題目及練習
text: 研究指出，一項重要好處是為學生營造的氛圍。學生在學校通常只與一類成年人互動，就是老師。家長加入校園後，學生便能與其他成年人接觸。這種氛圍令學生在校內活動時更加放鬆，意味着較少抑鬱情緒，自然也較少焦慮。
